subject: Chemistry
title: Particles of Matter Are Continuously Moving
summary: An agarbatti's smell reaches the next room without a fan. The particles of matter never stop moving, and they move faster when it is hotter.

notes.title: 04 – Particles of Matter Are Continuously Moving

keyPoints: Particles of matter are **continuously moving**: they have **kinetic energy**.
Their intermixing on their own is **diffusion**.
Temperature ↑ → kinetic energy ↑ → particles move faster → diffusion faster.
Diffusion is fastest in gases, slower in liquids, slowest in solids.

blocks.p: The scent particles of a burning agarbatti move on their own into the **spaces between air particles** and spread to the next room. This intermixing is **diffusion**.

blocks.alt: Scent particles spreading among air particles from the kitchen to the next room
blocks.caption: No fan needed: the particles move by themselves.

blocks.alt: Ink spreading slowly in cold water and fast in hot water
blocks.caption: Hotter water, faster particles, faster spreading.

blocks.formula: Temperature ↑ → kinetic energy ↑ → speed of particles ↑ → diffusion faster

list: Hot food is smelt from far away; cold food only up close.
Perfume sprayed in one corner fills the room.
A crystal of potassium permanganate colours still water by itself.

quiz.q: The intermixing of particles of two kinds of matter on their own is called:
quiz.explain: That is the definition of diffusion.

quiz.q: Ink spreads faster in hot water because:
options: Particles have more kinetic energy and move faster
quiz.explain: Higher temperature gives the particles more kinetic energy, so they move and mix faster.

quiz.q: Arrange in increasing rate of diffusion:
quiz.explain: Particles move most freely in gases and least in solids.

quiz.q: The energy particles have because of their motion is:
quiz.explain: Energy of motion is kinetic energy.

simulation.reason: Changing the temperature and watching the same ink drop spread faster or slower is a cause-and-effect experiment students can repeat at will; the readouts tie it to particle speed.
simulation.objective: See how temperature changes the speed of particles and how fast an ink drop spreads.
instructions: Set the water temperature with the slider.
Press Drop ink and watch the particles spread.
Note the spread after a few seconds.
Reset, change the temperature and compare.
